summary: Use blackboard pattern for agent coordination instead of pipeline/message-passing
detail: Blackboard pattern lets agents self-select into work based on visible shared state. Broadcasting needs rather than routing messages avoids coupling agents to each other.

summary: All state stored as .jsonl and .json files in .twining/ directory — no external databases
detail: File-native storage means jq-queryable, git-diffable, no setup. JSONL for append-only streams (blackboard), JSON for indexed records (decisions, graph).

summary: Embeddings must be lazy-loaded and fall back gracefully to keyword search if ONNX/transformers fails
detail: Key constraint: embedding system is enhancement, not requirement. Lazy loading defers heavy init. Fallback to keyword search (substring matching) ensures all query tools work regardless.

summary: Use ULIDs for all entity IDs — temporally sortable, globally unique
detail: ULIDs are timestamp-prefixed so they sort chronologically, are globally unique without coordination, and are more readable than UUIDs.

summary: Decisions track commit hashes to link architectural choices to git history
detail: Enables twining_why to answer 'why was this commit made?' and twining_commits to find decisions by commit hash. Bridges the gap between decision rationale and actual code changes.

summary: PlanningBridge as separate engine module, not inline in ContextAssembler
detail: Keeps .planning/ parsing isolated, testable, and reusable. ContextAssembler receives PlanningBridge via constructor injection.

summary: Override: Direct fs calls in DecisionEngine for STATE.md sync — deliberate exception to storage-layer convention -- overridden by human
detail: False-positive conflict detection — STATE.md fs exception and commit tracking are orthogonal. Restoring to active.

summary: Direct fs calls in DecisionEngine for STATE.md sync — deliberate exception to storage-layer convention
detail: False-positive conflict detection — STATE.md fs exception and commit tracking are orthogonal. Restoring to active.

summary: Override: Build bottom-up: utils → storage → engine → embeddings → tools → server -- overridden by human
detail: False-positive conflict detection — build order and coordination pattern are orthogonal. Restoring to active.

summary: Build bottom-up: utils → storage → engine → embeddings → tools → server
detail: False-positive conflict detection — build order and coordination pattern are orthogonal. Restoring to active.

summary: Embedded HTTP dashboard using native Node.js http module, vanilla HTML/JS, cytoscape.js for graph, vis-timeline for timeline
detail: Serena MCP pattern proven: in-process HTTP server, vanilla frontend, polling updates. Native http module avoids Express dependency. Cytoscape.js (109KB) and vis-timeline (186KB) are mature, zero-framework graph/timeline libraries. No build step required for frontend.

summary: Triage of TWINING_ARCH_REVIEW.md — 7 valid gaps, 3 invalid/already-addressed, 3 partial
detail: Findings validated by reading actual implementation code via Serena. Scope-expansion items (divergences 5-6) are invalid because they were intentional milestone additions. Dashboard opt-out (CQ7) is partially invalid since env-var controls already exist. Pending-hooks (divergence 3) was explicitly deferred in project planning. The remaining 7 findings are confirmed real gaps.

summary: Expose delegation and handoff as MCP tools rather than removing dead CoordinationEngine code
detail: Code is already written, tested, and the engine is constructed at startup. Exposing it completes the coordination feature set and eliminates the dead-code smell. Removing would waste existing work.

summary: Agent integration architecture doc recommends Claude Code + Twining as primary path, blackboard over orchestrator
detail: Claude Code + Twining MCP scores 15/15 because Claude Code is both MCP host and SWE agent natively, Twining provides persistent shared state through standard MCP tools, and subagents inherit connections automatically. Blackboard coordination fits MCP's request/response model (no push channel for orchestrator assignment), survives context resets (decisions persist in files), and enables token-budgeted selective injection. Academic research (LbMAS 2025) validates blackboard outperforming orchestrator patterns for LLM agents.

summary: Add rigor framework: verify step in agent lifecycle, tested_by traceability, drift detection, checkable constraints
detail: The agent lifecycle needed a verify step as a deterministic edge between decide and handoff. Six mechanisms form a hierarchy from convention (tests pass) through low-effort additions (assembly tracking, tested_by queries) to new tooling (drift detection, checkable constraints). This relocates rigor from 'agents should follow the lifecycle' to 'the system makes failures visible when they don't.' The tested_by relation type already exists in the knowledge graph but was unused — activating it is the highest-leverage change.

summary: Implement drift detection via git log and sandboxed constraint checking via execSync
detail: Git log provides file modification timestamps and commit hashes with minimal overhead. execSync with timeout and shell operator rejection provides sandboxed execution. Both follow the existing VerifyEngine pattern of returning structured check results.

summary: Create comprehensive demo video plan with realistic multi-agent scenario
detail: Demo should follow a narrative arc showing how agents use Twining throughout a realistic development workflow. Better to show the "why" (solving real coordination problems) rather than just feature enumeration. Will use a multi-agent scenario where agents coordinate on adding authentication to a web app, demonstrating blackboard, decisions, knowledge graph, context assembly, verification, and handoffs.

summary: Build automated demo using playwright browser automation + screenshot capture + narration script
detail: Will create: (1) demo project with real code, (2) automation script that executes Twining commands to populate data, (3) playwright automation to navigate dashboard and capture screenshots, (4) HTML presentation combining screenshots with narration that can be screen-recorded or converted to video with ffmpeg. This approach is fully automated and produces a professional result.

summary: Switch execGit to execFileSync with argument arrays; replace broken shell operator blocklist with newline/null-byte validation
detail: execFileSync with argument arrays eliminates shell injection entirely for git commands. For constraint commands, shell features like pipes are intentional (documented in CLAUDE.md). The real threat vectors are newlines and null bytes that could inject additional commands. Added 1000-char length limit as defense-in-depth.

summary: Fix race conditions by using single index lock for atomic file+index updates in DecisionStore and HandoffStore
detail: Using a single index lock for the entire read-modify-write cycle ensures both the individual JSON file and the index are always consistent. The index lock is the natural serialization point since all queries go through the index. For HandoffStore, direct fs reads/writes inside the lock avoid nested locking (since writeJSONL/readJSONL have their own internal locks).

summary: Move archive file writes inside blackboard lock to prevent data loss on crash
detail: Write-ahead pattern: entries are written to archive first, then removed from blackboard, all under the same lock. This ensures entries always exist in at least one location. Uses direct fs.appendFileSync instead of appendJSONL to avoid nested locking.

summary: Fix token budget accounting: warnings get priority access to full budget, non-warnings capped at 90%
detail: Warnings fill first from the full budget (priority access). Non-warnings are capped at 90% of the budget to ensure warnings can always get in. This preserves the intent (warnings get priority) while handling edge cases (small budgets where 10% can't hold any entry).

summary: Add project name to dashboard title/header and GitHub icon link — fixes #2 and #3
detail: Project name is already available via path.basename(projectRoot) in api-routes.ts. Adding it to the /api/status response and rendering it in the header h1 + page title is the minimal change. GitHub icon uses the standard octicon SVG inline to avoid extra dependencies.

summary: Three-layer analytics: local value stats, tool call instrumentation via registerTool patch, opt-in PostHog telemetry
detail: Layer 1 (value stats) computes from existing .twining/ data with zero new collection. Layer 2 (tool instrumentation) patches registerTool on McpServer instance before tool registration — zero changes to 8 tool files. Layer 3 (PostHog telemetry) is opt-in only, SHA-256 hashed identity, dynamic import for graceful degradation. This separation keeps privacy-sensitive code isolated and makes each layer independently testable.

summary: Add twining_dismiss tool for targeted removal of blackboard entries by ID
detail: Added dismiss at three layers: BlackboardStore.dismiss (lock, read, filter, rewrite with proper-lockfile), BlackboardEngine.dismiss (delegates to store, cleans up embeddings), and twining_dismiss tool (accepts ids array + optional reason). Follows the same lock-read-rewrite pattern as the archiver. The reason parameter is accepted but not stored — it serves as documentation in the tool call itself.

summary: Add CI (build-and-test on PRs) and Publish (npm publish on tags) GitHub Actions workflows
detail: CI workflow gates PRs with Node 18/20/22 matrix (minimum supported, current LTS, active release). Publish workflow triggers on v* tags with npm provenance attestations and auto-generated GitHub Releases. POSTHOG_API_KEY is injected only during publish builds. workflow_dispatch with dry-run option enables testing the pipeline without publishing. Tests re-run in publish as defense-in-depth since tag pushes bypass PR CI.

summary: Implement Twining as a Claude Code plugin with skills, hooks, agents, commands, and MCP server instructions
detail: Plugin provides one-step install, behavioral teaching via skills (not just documentation), auto-starting MCP server, and lifecycle hooks. Skills are mapped to cover all 27 tools across 7 skills. MCP server instructions provide a fallback for non-Claude-Code clients.

summary: Redesign dashboard UI with dark-first professional theme using Sora/DM Sans/JetBrains Mono fonts and teal accent color
detail: Dark-first design matches developer tool context (terminal/IDE environments). Sora provides geometric, modern headings; DM Sans is clean and readable for body text; JetBrains Mono is the definitive developer monospace font. Teal accent (#00d4aa) is distinctive without being generic blue. CSS custom properties throughout enable easy theming and extension.

summary: Prevent duplicate browser tabs by checking health endpoint before auto-opening
detail: If the server bound to a different port than configured (port !== config.port), check the original port's health endpoint for a 'twining-mcp' server signature. If found, skip auto-open. This is non-blocking (1s timeout) and gracefully handles the case without requiring cross-process coordination.

summary: Show session-ended overlay after 3 consecutive poll failures instead of attempting window.close()
detail: Track wasConnected and disconnectCount state. After 3 consecutive failed polls (~9 seconds), show a fullscreen overlay saying 'Session Ended' with blur backdrop. This avoids false positives from transient network issues while giving clear feedback. window.close() is attempted as a best-effort fallback.

summary: Fix Stop hook to return required JSON decision format for Claude Code validation
detail: Claude Code Stop hooks with type 'prompt' must return a JSON response with a decision field. Added explicit instruction at the end of the prompt telling the LLM to return {decision: approve, reason: Twining housekeeping complete} after completing its tasks.

summary: Pure bash version bump script with sed for plugin version management
detail: Bash + sed has zero dependencies, works on macOS and Linux, and keeps the script simple. Reads current version from plugin.json as source of truth, supports both exact versions and patch/minor/major auto-increment.

summary: CI job to enforce plugin version bumps on PRs that change plugin/ files
detail: Added plugin-version-check job that only runs on PRs (not pushes to main, since direct commits happen). Uses git diff to detect plugin/ changes and checks both version files for version line changes. Excludes plugin.json itself from the "changed files" check to avoid false positives when only the version is bumped.

summary: Skip ONNX embedding initialization in test environment via process.env.VITEST check
detail: Single check in doInitialize() for process.env.VITEST (set automatically by Vitest) enables fallback mode immediately. Zero test file changes needed, all 11 failing test files fixed, production behavior unchanged. Test suite dropped from ~3 minutes to ~6 seconds.

summary: Stop hook uses line-number comparison for per-commit Twining coverage instead of session-wide counts
detail: Compare line numbers of last Edit/Write call vs last twining_decide/post/verify/handoff call in the transcript. If the last code change comes after the last Twining recording, block. Same pure bash+grep approach, no new dependencies — just grep -n with tail -1 instead of grep -c.

summary: Fix timeline zoom by changing overflow:auto to overflow:hidden and add zoom controls toolbar
detail: overflow:hidden lets vis-timeline handle all scroll/zoom internally without interference. Added explicit zoom controls (zoom in/out, fit all, jump to now) as a secondary zoom mechanism so users are never stuck. Also added domain swim lanes, domain filter chips, gradient confidence-coded items, custom dark tooltips, and entrance animations for visual polish.

summary: Replace search bar multi-select with toggle chips, add search icon, and style filters to match toolbar design language
detail: Toggle chips match the filter pattern used in timeline domain filters and graph type filters, providing a consistent UX. Pill-shaped input with embedded search/clear icons is more modern. Custom-styled select and labeled date inputs improve visual cohesion. All changes are CSS/HTML/JS only with no new dependencies.

summary: Add Stream View as alternate visualization for Blackboard tab
detail: A vertical card-based activity stream best fits the conversational nature of blackboard data. Cards colored by entry type, grouped by time, with CSS thread lines for relates_to connections. Visually distinct from Timeline (horizontal time bands) and Graph (node network). Scales well for dozens-to-hundreds of entries kept active by archival.

summary: Add twining_register MCP tool and subagent coordination integration (dispatch skill, SubagentStop hook, aware-worker agent)
detail: Exposed agentStore.upsert() as twining_register tool (matching existing coordination tool patterns), created a dispatch skill to teach the protocol, added SubagentStop hook as safety net, and created twining-aware-worker agent template for subagents that use Twining directly. This bridges the gap between Agent tool dispatch and Twining coordination with minimal source changes (one new tool, ~40 lines).

summary: Include projectRoot in health endpoint to distinguish same-project vs different-project dashboard instances
detail: Adding projectRoot to the health response lets isExistingDashboard() distinguish same-project dashboards (safe to skip, since they read from the same .twining/ on disk) from different-project dashboards (should auto-open a new tab). This is minimally invasive — only the health response and the dedup check change.

summary: Demo uses claude -p with explicit tool-call prompts for deterministic behavior
detail: Each claude -p prompt explicitly lists the tool calls and parameters the agent should execute. This ensures deterministic, reproducible demo runs — the agent doesn't need to reason about what to do, it just executes the prescribed calls. The alternative of letting the agent explore freely would produce inconsistent results across recordings.

summary: Separate persistent dashboard server from claude -p tool processes for demo recordings
detail: A standalone start-dashboard.sh runs one persistent MCP server for the dashboard HTTP endpoint. The claude -p processes disable their dashboard entirely (TWINING_DASHBOARD=0). Both read/write the same .twining/ files on disk. Dashboard stays live the whole time, no port conflicts, no reconnect flicker.

summary: Implement Playwright-based demo orchestrator replacing manual shell + tab-switching workflow
detail: Playwright provides headless/headed browser control with built-in video recording, DOM injection for overlays, and programmatic tab/view switching. Using tsx for direct TypeScript execution avoids a separate build step. Data-driven tab switching (polling stat elements) is more reliable than hardcoded delays since claude -p execution time varies.

summary: Add standard open source community files for public announcement readiness
detail: GitHub community standards require CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, issue templates, and PR template. Also fixing telemetry default contradiction and adding engines field.

summary: v1.4 milestone: Behavioral spec + eval harness + plugin tuning as single release
detail: All three phases must ship together — a spec alone isn't a release, a harness without a spec has nothing to measure, and tuning without a harness is guesswork. The spec lives at plugin/BEHAVIORS.md since it primarily guides plugin development. Dual eval approach: LLM-as-judge for synthetic scenarios + transcript analysis of real dogfooding sessions.

summary: Behavioral spec as single Markdown document parsed by state machine into typed objects
detail: A single BEHAVIORS.md in plugin/ serves as both human documentation and eval input. A state-machine parser in test/eval/ transforms it into typed BehaviorSpec objects using shared Zod-validated interfaces. This avoids duplicating behavioral rules in code and keeps the spec authoritative.

summary: Eval scenarios use flat tool call lists with per-scorer pass/fail expectations
detail: Flat tool lists are simpler to write and maintain. Scorers infer patterns from sequences rather than relying on annotated step metadata. Per-scorer expectations (vs single pass/fail) allow scenarios to test mixed quality -- good sequencing but bad scope, for example.

summary: 7 category scorers with hybrid rule mapping: metadata from BehaviorSpec, custom check logic inline
detail: Category scorers (sequencing, scope quality, argument quality, decision hygiene, workflow completeness, anti-patterns, quality criteria) group logically. Hybrid approach gives traceability back to BEHAVIORS.md rule IDs while allowing sophisticated check logic that can't be expressed as rule strings. Scorers return both numeric 0-1 and pass/fail checks for thresholds and diagnostics respectively.

summary: Eval harness uses matrix testing: 22 scenarios × 7 scorers = 154 dynamic vitest tests
detail: Matrix approach (each scenario tested against every scorer) maximizes coverage and catches cross-category regressions. YAML scenarios are data-driven so adding new cases requires no code. Separate vitest config isolates eval runs from the main 700-test suite.

summary: Scorers use weighted severity aggregation: MUST fail=0, SHOULD fail=0.5, pass=1 with DEFAULT_THRESHOLD=0.8
detail: Weighted aggregation via aggregateChecks helper gives MUST/MUST_NOT checks veto power (score 0) while SHOULD checks degrade gracefully (0.5). Threshold of 0.8 means a scenario can fail one SHOULD check and still pass, but any MUST failure is an automatic fail. Rule IDs trace to BEHAVIORS.md for auditability.

summary: Transcript parser extracts both tool_use calls and tool_result blocks, follows subagent parentUuid chains
detail: Capturing tool results alongside calls provides richer data for Phase 18 LLM-as-judge scoring. Including subagent calls captures the full picture of Twining usage since twining-aware-worker agents make most tool calls.

summary: Segment transcripts into workflow chunks and extend NormalizedToolCall with optional result field
detail: Workflow segmentation gives granular per-workflow scores rather than one blunt session score. Extending NormalizedToolCall with optional result field is backward-compatible — existing scorers ignore it, Phase 18 LLM judge uses it.

summary: Separate vitest config and npm script for transcript evals with manifest-based fixture discovery
detail: Separate config keeps synthetic and transcript runs independent per success criteria. Manifest file allows annotating fixtures with metadata (description, expected quality) for richer reporting vs bare glob discovery.

summary: Transcript parser uses two-pass JSONL extraction with workflow segmentation at twining_assemble boundaries
detail: Two-pass extraction (first collect tool_use, then match tool_result) handles the JSONL structure where calls and results are in separate messages. Segmentation at twining_assemble boundaries creates natural workflow units matching how agents actually work. MCP name normalization via split('__').pop() handles both prefix patterns observed in real transcripts.

summary: Transcript eval uses 0.6 threshold (vs 0.8 for synthetic) with aggregate average assertions instead of per-scorer
detail: Lower threshold (0.6) accounts for real-world messiness while still differentiating good vs poor sessions. Aggregate average assertions (rather than per-scorer) prevent flaky tests from natural variance in individual dimensions. Phase 19 will tune thresholds with more data.

summary: Category-aware scorer filtering eliminates false positives instead of modifying plugin skills
detail: The failures were scorer precision issues, not plugin instruction gaps. Fixing scorers to respect scenario categories (only checking sequencing/completeness for the workflow matching the scenario's declared category) is more correct than warping plugin instructions to avoid triggering cross-category checks.

summary: Regression baseline captures full eval state as JSON for CI comparison
detail: A structured JSON baseline with per-scenario scores, thresholds, holdout results, and token budget enables automated CI comparison. The generator script (regression-baseline.ts) is rerunnable so baselines can be refreshed after intentional changes.

summary: Fix LLM judge model ID and increase eval timeouts for LLM scorer runs
detail: Updated model to claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (current Haiku). Increased eval timeout to 60s (synthetic — most scenarios need only 2-8s per LLM call) and transcript timeout to 120s (real transcripts have many more tool calls requiring many more judge API calls).

summary: Use current live session as third eval fixture — captures post-instruction-fix behavior for A/B comparison
detail: Using the live session transcript captures real dogfooding behavior with the updated instructions. Adding it as a third 'good' fixture provides an A/B comparison: session-good-workflow (pre-fix) vs this session (post-fix). The scrub script already handles in-progress JSONL files correctly since it processes line-by-line. Three fixtures (2 good, 1 poor) give better signal than two.

summary: No git tag for v1.4 — plugin-only milestones don't get npm release tags
detail: Git tags (v1.x.x) are reserved for npm MCP server releases that trigger CI/CD publish. Plugin milestones are internal development milestones that don't correspond to npm version bumps.

summary: Enforce mandatory agent registration and handoff in plugin v1.1.5
detail: Changed REGISTER rules from SHOULD to MUST, added GEN-01 through GEN-04 general principles prioritizing task completion, updated PreToolUse hook to require registration before assembly, enhanced stop-hook to block exit without handoff after code changes, and updated orient/handoff skills to reflect mandatory registration and handoff workflows.

summary: Auto-populate knowledge graph from tool calls via GraphAutoPopulator
detail: Centralizing auto-extraction in GraphAutoPopulator removes manual overhead while making the graph useful. Each engine method (decide, post, handoff, linkCommit, register, reconsider, override) calls the populator after its primary operation. All calls are try/catch wrapped — graph is an optimization layer, not correctness requirement.

summary: Replace computeGraphConnectivity with computeGraphReachability using typed BFS and adaptive weight fallback
detail: Typed BFS traversal follows specific relation types (decided_by, affects, depends_on, etc.) with depth-based path scoring and relation type bonuses. Adaptive weight fallback redistributes the 35% graph weight proportionally when all graph scores are 0, preventing score compression for sparse/empty graphs. Relevance paths annotate assembled decisions with how they were found.

summary: Reduce default tool surface from 32 to 16 via full_surface config flag
detail: Gating rarely-used tools behind tools.full_surface config (default false) reduces context overhead while keeping all tools available for power users. Each tool registration checks the flag individually, so no code is deleted and the change is fully reversible via config.

summary: Assemble output includes structured markdown briefing and inline status summary
detail: formatForLLM() produces imperative markdown sections (decisions to respect, warnings, continue from, quick reference) optimized for LLM consumption. assembleWithStatus() merges status summary into the assemble call, eliminating a separate tool call. Both changes reduce turns and improve information utilization.

summary: Graph auto-population disabled by default (opt-in via graph.auto_populate config)
detail: Setting auto_populate to false by default removes overhead with zero measured downside. Graph tools remain available for manual use. Users who want auto-population can enable it in config.yml.

summary: Coordination effectiveness test suite using real stores with temp dirs, no mocking
detail: Real stores (BlackboardStore, DecisionStore, HandoffStore, AgentStore, GraphEngine) with temp dirs give accurate end-to-end coverage of the assemble pipeline. Only SearchEngine is null (no embeddings needed). This catches real integration issues that mocks would hide, while still running in ~1 second.

summary: Reorder formatForLLM: warnings first, then handoffs, then decisions, then needs, then findings
detail: Warnings (what NOT to do) are the most behavior-changing signal. Handoffs provide continuation context. Decisions are important but less urgent. Findings are background. This ordering front-loads the most actionable information into the first 500 tokens where agents are most likely to act on it.

summary: Enrich handoff data in AssembledContext to include individual results for detailed checklists
detail: Loading full HandoffRecord (via handoffStore.get) costs one file read per handoff (max 5) but provides structured results with status icons ([x], [ ], [BLOCKED]) that give agents an actionable checklist of what to continue.

summary: Filter redundant findings that substantially overlap with decision summaries in formatForLLM
detail: Substring overlap check (first 30 chars of lowercase summary) catches the common case where a finding is promoted to a decision. Non-overlapping findings are preserved. This is conservative — only filters obvious duplicates.

summary: Empty-state short-circuit in formatForLLM returns terse one-liner when no content exists
detail: When there are no warnings, decisions, findings, needs, handoffs, or questions, the full markdown template is pure noise. A terse 'No prior context for scope: X' eliminates this overhead completely.

summary: Bug-investigation resolution scorer penalizes redundant re-fixes when Agent A already completed the work
detail: Verifying completed work (50 pts) should score higher than redundantly redoing it (20 pts). This directly measures whether coordination tools help agents avoid wasted rework, which is the core value proposition of Twining.

summary: Add assumptions field to Decision type for assumption-based validation in assemble output
detail: Explicit assumptions let formatForLLM be prescriptive when assumptions hold ('follow exactly') and advisory when they don't ('reconsider'). This bridges the gap between structured decision records and actionable implementation guidance.

summary: Add FILES TO CHECK BEFORE WRITING section to formatForLLM output
detail: Explicit read directives as a checklist (Read src/events/bus.ts) push agents to open files before writing, improving pattern consistency and context recovery scores.

summary: Assumption validation in assembler: check findings/warnings/decisions against decision assumptions
detail: Lightweight term-matching with negation detection. Extracts key terms from assumptions, checks if evidence corpus contains those terms near negation words (not, no longer, changed, replaced, removed, etc). Challenged assumptions get RECONSIDER directive in formatForLLM; unchallenged get 'follow exactly'. No LLM call needed — pure heuristic keeps it fast.

summary: Include constraints and rejected alternatives in assembled decision output for pattern propagation
detail: Constraints like 'All services must use EventBus.emit()' and rejected alternatives like 'Direct calls: tight coupling' give agents concrete directives about what to do and what not to do. This bridges the gap between abstract decision summaries and actionable implementation guidance.

summary: Sprint-simulation scenario: 12-session sprint with requirement change for long-horizon coordination testing
detail: 12 sessions from 3 engineer personas with heterogeneous tasks (features, bugs, refactoring) and a mid-sprint requirement change (session 8: SMS added, invalidating email-only assumption from session 3). This tests decision persistence, assumption validation, cross-feature interference, and context recovery at realistic scale. Scores 5 dimensions including assumptionHandling which directly measures Twining's RECONSIDER mechanism.

summary: Filter out entry_type "decision" blackboard entries in assembler to prevent type confusion
detail: Filter at the assembler's entry-loading step (both scope-match and semantic-merge paths) rather than at the blackboard store level. The blackboard schema allows entry_type "decision" for backwards compatibility, but the assembler must not treat them as Decision objects. Filtering here is defensive — it protects against data that already exists and any future misuse.

summary: Add SessionStart command hook to inject Twining Lifecycle Gates into project CLAUDE.md
detail: Shell script runs before the prompt hook, checks for marker string 'Twining Lifecycle Gates', appends condensed 3-gate section if absent. Pure bash, no dependencies, 5s timeout. Creates CLAUDE.md if it doesn't exist. The content is a condensed version of docs/CLAUDE_TEMPLATE.md covering just the mandatory gates and critical rules.

summary: Remove fullSurface tool gate — all 34 MCP tools always registered
detail: Claude Code already defers MCP tool loading via ToolSearch — tool schemas are only loaded into context when needed. The fullSurface gate was premature optimization that actively broke mandatory functionality. Per Anthropic's tool context management docs, tool search is the correct pattern for large toolsets, and we already have it.

summary: Layered instruction architecture: CLAUDE.md as authority, lean SessionStart prompt, third-person skill descriptions
detail: CLAUDE.md is the single source of truth for gate definitions (persistent, survives context compression). SessionStart prompt is now a 40-token pointer to CLAUDE.md. Skills focus on HOW-TO workflows with third-person descriptions and when-to-use triggers for discovery. MCP instructions remain as condensed fallback for non-plugin clients.

summary: Default tool surface is 5 core tools (assemble, record, post, why, housekeeping); all other tools remain gated behind full_surface: true in config
detail: supersedes the prior 'remove fullSurface gate / register all 34' direction

summary: Bug-investigation benchmark uses assertion-based tests rather than numeric scoring
detail: the prior decision describing a 50/20 point resolution scorer was never landed in code

summary: Default tool surface is 5 core tools gated behind full_surface flag
detail: supersedes prior decision describing 16-tool default, which was itself later changed in commit dc2d7ac to the narrower 5-tool core

summary: Prefer explicit Rationale:/Why:/Reason:/Because: markers over heuristic split separators in record-parser
detail: prior behavior misfired on mid-sentence 'as'/'since'/'because', causing summary and rationale to bleed. Alternative rejected: removing heuristic separators entirely (would break 'Chose X

summary: Replaced split(regex, 2) with single-split-on-first-match that preserves the full remainder
detail: rationale

summary: Sliced decision cross-post summary to 200 chars and wrapped in try/catch inside DecisionEngine.decide
detail: blackboard enforces summary <=200, and the decision file is already persisted by the time cross-post runs. Without the slice, decide() would throw after the write, leaving the file on disk but record-tools returning decisions_created: []. The slice preserves the blackboard surface while the unbounded full text stays in the decision JSON and in the detail field.

summary: Surfaced per-decision persistence errors in the twining_record response
detail: decision_errors rather than swallowing them silently

summary: Chose two specs over one combined spec
detail: Spec A (issues #8/#9/#10, plugin hygiene) ships fast as one plugin patch release; Spec B (issue #7, decision/scope GC) gets its own design pass because it has substantively different design surface

summary: Chose to keep CLAUDE.md gate authority over reporter's prompt-injection-only alternative for issue #9
detail: CLAUDE.md persists in system context every turn and survives compaction, while prompt-injected SessionStart content gets summarized away. Empirical evidence from prior testing showed Claude was finicky about calling twining_record without CLAUDE.md anchor. No new data shows that has changed; risk-asymmetric move is to keep authority. Filed follow-up to benchmark this on current models.

summary: Chose broad marker search across 4 files (~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, project CLAUDE.md, project CLAUDE.local.md, project .claude/CLAUDE.local.md) plus opt-out flag .twining/.no-claude-md-gates for issue #9
detail: covers reporter's exact setup and provides explicit user-controlled escape hatch. Rejected env-var-only opt-out because flag files are project-scoped, visible in ls, and survive shell-environment differences across team members.

summary: Chose two-layer disable for TWINING_DISABLED (hooks no-op + MCP server early-exit before tool registration)
detail: single layer at the server only would still leave hooks firing pre-commit blocks complaining about missing twining_record calls. Two layers gives invisible behavior. Rejected mid-session toggle scope per reporter answer (scenario 2 only).

summary: Chose to convert SessionStart prompt-type hook to command-type hook for issue #8
detail: command hooks emit additionalContext JSON without needing ToolUseContext that resume sessions don't supply. Rejected narrowing matcher to startup-only because resume is exactly when the gate reminder is most useful. Rejected dropping the prompt hook entirely because it loses the moment-of-session signal.

summary: Chose Vitest with child_process.spawnSync for hook tests over bats/shell-only
detail: keeps everything in the existing test runner so npm test catches hook regressions, and avoids introducing a new test dependency. Single shared test/hooks/run-hook.ts helper keeps hook tests DRY.

summary: Chose to phase the work as: verifications first → test helper → server gate → simple hook guards → ensure-claude-md-gates (compound changes) → SessionStart command hook → versions → manual smoke test
detail: Chose to phase the work as: verifications first → test helper → server gate → simple hook guards → ensure-claude-md-gates (compound changes) → SessionStart command hook → versions → manual smoke test → release. Foundation-first ordering means each phase's tests can rely on infrastructure from prior phases.

detail: ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md tends to be small). Implementation chose project-first because hit-rate ordering matters more than read-cost: most users have the marker in a project CLAUDE.md or project .claude/CLAUDE.local.md, so project-first short-circuits faster in the common case. summary: Rewrote server-startup test discrimination from signal/exit-code to stderr content. Empirical observation: with EOF stdin, both gate-firing and gate-not-firing exit with code 0 (no signal), but only t
detail: Rewrote server-startup test discrimination from signal/exit-code to stderr content. Empirical observation: with EOF stdin, both gate-firing and gate-not-firing exit with code 0 (no signal), but only the gate-not-firing path produces [twining] stderr output (dashboard startup, config warnings). The signal-based test was attempting to keep stdin open with a Readable.pipe to force SIGTERM on timeout, but Linux closes the pipe early when the source Readable enters end state. Stderr-content discrimination is platform-independent and 10x faster (343ms vs 3155ms). Rejected: increasing test timeout (doesn't fix root cause), holding stdin open differently with raw fd manipulation (fragile, more code).
